headline: Highest risk is medium: caveman’s MCP-enabled content-writing workflow can feed LightZero no direct write path, so prompt injection and cascading errors are plausible but bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project notes and CLAUDE.md, so attacker-controlled content could enter its outputs. LightZero has no MCP or filesystem read/write, so direct automated ingestion is not documented; the pairwise bridge is therefore inferred, not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman’s MCP target exposes untrusted content into its prompt context
IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that forwards caveman output into game logic or prompts
mitigations: Disable MCP for caveman in this pairing
Restrict caveman to a read-only workspace
Add a manual review step before any caveman output is reused
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but LightZero has no documented filesystem read, write, or network egress. That makes shared-data leakage plausible only through unusual external wiring, and the blast radius is limited because LightZero itself does not ingest files by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies caveman logs or notes into LightZero inputs
IF an external wrapper grants LightZero filesystem access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep caveman logs out of shared folders
Run LightZero in a separate account or container
Review any copied text before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman has no documented write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or shell execution, while LightZero explicitly lacks filesystem write and git modification. With no overlapping mutable surface, a write-write conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents shared write access not present in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant shared git credentials
Avoid external wrappers that add write permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and other text that could be treated as authoritative by downstream tooling, while LightZero is a game-playing system with no documented verification layer. The pairwise pathway is indirect, but if LightZero consumes caveman output through an orchestrator, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or decisions.
conditions: IF LightZero receives caveman-generated text as input without validation
IF an orchestrator uses caveman outputs as ground truth for LightZero decisions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of caveman output
Log source provenance for every transferred artifact
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. caveman lists general project-note and log data classes, and LightZero lists none, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into caveman or LightZero outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in either agent
requires-engineering: document retention and deletion policies
